newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rebels overrun police post, kill 24.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rebels overrun police post, kill 24.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels overran an isolated police post in Sri Lanka's northeast early on Thursday killing 24 policemen, defence officials said.
A large group of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels stormed the Kudapokuna police post, just north of Welikanda, 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo, before dawn, they said.
"The entire post was overrun," said a defence official.
It was not immediately clear if there were any casualties among the rebels, who are fighting for independence for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.

It is the second time in three days that the rebels attacked police. Suspected Tamil Tigers on Tuesday hurled hand grenades at a police vehicle in a crowded market in the army-controlled northern town of Vavuniya, killing at least two policemen.
More than a dozen people, including several police who were working undercover, were wounded in the attack. Vavuniya is just south of the northern mainland area controlled by the LTTE.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
